blocks.heading: Closest Call Between the Two Categories

items.text: IT and software hiring is closer to a tie than people assume
Top-tier IITs capture the "alpha" ultra-high offers, but top private colleges like VIT Vellore run 900+ recruiters a year and generate a much larger volume of solid mid-range offers.
Core engineering still leans government

blocks.sourceSectionTitle: Engineering: the closest call between the two categories

items.text: The hiring market has moved since the days when a college's category alone decided your shortlist odds.
IT and tech hiring in particular now weights technical assessments and visible project work heavily over degree pedigree for many entry-level roles.

This does not erase the category gap entirely - it just means the gap is smaller for many roles than it was a decade ago, and it keeps shrinking further the more visible proof of skill you bring on top of whichever college you attend.
Run any specific government-vs-private choice in front of you through these three checks, in order.
How much does your specific field reward the government label.
Software-focused engineering and mid-tier management reward it far less.

blocks.heading: Government Side That Rarely Gets Named

items.text: Nearly one in three sanctioned teaching posts sits vacant across India's higher-education system - check the specific college's actual faculty strength, not the sanctioned count.
Remote-location state universities often struggle hardest to fill vacant faculty positions, which can mean thinner mentorship for years at a stretch.
Not every government college gets industry recruiter visits - some carry the "government" label with almost no active placement pipeline.
Bond requirements at some government medical and other professional colleges can restrict immediate postgraduate or career flexibility after graduation.

blocks.sourceSectionTitle: The hidden risk on the government side that rarely gets named

blocks.heading: Verify a Specific College Before You Decide

items.text: Ask for branch-wise, year-wise median salary data in writing, not a single highlighted "highest package" figure or a vague overall placement percentage with no breakdown.

Check the college's NIRF Graduation Outcomes (GO) score specifically, not just its overall rank - this is the component that reflects placement rates and median salaries most directly, though remember much of the underlying data is self-reported by the institution.

Verify recognition directly on the official portal - UGC for general universities, AICTE for technical colleges, NMC for medical colleges, or the Bar Council of India for law schools - rather than trusting a claim on the college's own website.

Talk to two or three recent graduates directly, not just students the admission office introduces you to, and ask specifically what role and salary they actually accepted, not what the college reported.

Check faculty vacancy and recruiter visit history for the exact branch or specialisation you plan to study, since both figures vary enormously even within a single college depending on the department.
Weigh the fee against a strict budget benchmark, not against the campus.
